finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If filePath contains a malicious path or filename, it could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The _rootDir variable is assumed to be a trusted directory path. The filePath variable is assumed to be attacker-controlled.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the reported vulnerability (CWE-78: OS Command Injection) is not applicable in this context. The filePath variable is used to construct file paths, not to execute OS commands.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the filePath variable is used to construct file paths, not to execute OS commands. The code does not involve any OS command execution, so there is no risk of OS command injection.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is File.WriteAllText, which only writes to a file and does not invoke an OS shell. Verified that Path.Combine(_rootDir, filePath, fileName) simply concatenates path segments; if filePath is absolute it overrides _rootDir, but this is a path traversal issue, not command injection. No code performs a system call or shell execution based on filePath.
